steps.name: Young-sounding Voice
steps.text: What do you want to show me?

steps.name: Resolute Voice
steps.text: Pick up the pace a little, we'll be there soon.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: If you walk in the snow by the stream, the fragrant plum blossoms are rare. However, you can find some at the base of the mountain.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I suppose the view of the fireworks against the city skyline from atop the mountain could be the only thing worth climbing all the way up here.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Fireworks? Who cares about those?! I brought you here to see... this pine tree.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: An evergreen... It can withstand the cold weather.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: No. That's not what's special about it.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: I planted this tree myself, right before I assumed my post in Baizao. Back then, I had the same mindset as you.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: After all these years, I'm a different person now, and this tree is a different tree.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I do not understand.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: That doesn't matter. All you need to do now is look at the tree; imprint it in your memory.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Qingyan, you will do well in the Judicial Review Office. You will go on to be an excellent Deputy Minister or maybe a minister yourself!

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Those cases will not be a problem for you. There's really only one issue that you'll need to focus on—

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Will you be able to handle the truth?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I do not understand.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: You don't need to understand now. Every once in a while, you will think back to this pine tree. Once you've spent enough time contemplating the tree, you will understand the rest.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: After I die, cut down the tree. Use its wood to fashion my coffin.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Mr. Yu...

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: We should be going. The higher you climb, the colder it gets.

a.text: Years of wind and snow, moments fleeting like blossoms in the morning and evening light.
Once more, I think back to the pine tree and the mountain path, buried in snow.
Yu Cheng, what penalty do you propose to atone for your guilt?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: (snoring softly)

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: *cough* *cough*

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Huh? What time is it? Has the suspect confessed yet?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Censor Jie Zhen, this is a serious matter. Please mind your words and behavior.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: This is a routine internal matter for the Judicial Review Office. The Department of Discipline and Supervision is just going through the motions. It's not a big deal.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: However, this trial today certainly has been interesting. The minister is usually quite well-tempered. I've never seen her that angry before.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Yu Cheng, you served in the Judicial Review Office once. You took an oath before the bronze mirror.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Do you really think the Judicial Review Office is the proper place for you to act like a spoiled brat?!

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: That's an unjust accusation. You asked me all that you needed to ask, and I answered them. What else would you have me do?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: On the fifteenth of last month, around 1:45 AM, someone set fire to the southern end of the Judicial Review Office scrollery. That person was me.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Liar! When the fire broke out, you were in pre-trial detention. How could you have started it?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: If you planned the fire, you had help. Name your co-conspirator.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: I had no co-conspirator. However, I did have a helper.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: A fowlbeast.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: That night, a wounded fowlbeast landed by the window of my cell. I fed it a few grains of rice and some fresh water.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: The fowlbeast was quite intelligent. I saved it, and it was willing to return the favor. I gave it a burning straw and told it to fly to the scrollery.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Whaa???

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: *cough* *cough*

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Yu Cheng, the courtroom has no time for your games!

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: I'm not playing games. Ask me anything, and I will answer truthfully.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Very well. You say you started the fire. Elaborate on that, if you will.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: What species of fowlbeast was it that you used?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Do I look like a fowlbeast expert? I only remember that it was completely black, without a single stray hair... as black as the human heart.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: You said you gave the fowlbeast a burning straw. You were locked in a cell. Where did you get the straw?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: I picked it out of my sleeping cushion.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Your cushion was made of cotton.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Then my memory is mistaken. It must have fallen in from the fowlbeast's nest.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: The guards did a full search of your cell after the fire. They did not find any fowlbeast nest.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: If criminals didn't try to cover their tracks, we wouldn't need the Judicial Review Office or the Ministry of Justice, would we?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: That fowlbeast truly understood human nature.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Why you...

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Oh, right, as for how I lit the straw in the first place—I struck the cell bars with these iron shackles exactly eight hundred sixty-three times, one for each year of the Judicial Review Office's existence.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: That is as much detail as I can provide on the fire. Will it do?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Madam Minister, do you have more questions for me?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: It seems that he has been reading some fanciful stories since his retirement.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: This is no time for jokes.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Well, she had the patience to play along with him and indulge his insanity.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Do you want to enter this line into the record?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: ...Of course.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Interesting...

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Yu Cheng was once appointed Deputy Minister for the Judicial Review Office's Haoran Pavilion. There, he took down countless corrupt mandarins and notorious criminals.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: However, after his retirement, you convicted him of fabricating evidence, which is how he ended up here.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: As you think back now, do you regret your choice, Deputy Minister Lin?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: The law is the law. It bends for no man. Stop trying to stir up trouble, Censor Jie.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: But when we look at it, Yu Cheng's behavior is quite odd. When he was charged with fabricating evidence, he did not question it or protest. Now, after he's been convicted, he decides to start a fire?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: That's not right...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I still have questions!

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Yes, Deputy Minister Lin?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: ...Hmph.
Lin Qingyan puts down her pen and paper and happens to meet Yu Cheng's gaze. The prisoner, who has been pretending to be insane, is now staring at her intently.
She wants to know the truth. She does not fear revealing herself in the process.
Yu Cheng seems pleased with Lin Qingyan's reaction. He closes his eyes, as an ugly grin crosses his face.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Deputy Minister Lin, as acting clerk, you need only take notes.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Minister Chen, there is one question you haven't yet asked. Yu Cheng claims he set the fire. What was his motive?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: The suspect's confession is clearly nonsense. Why bother asking his motive?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Hahaha. I am the one who set fire to the scrollery. You must believe me.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: As for why I did it...

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Yu Cheng!

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: There were seventy-four thousand case files in the southern section of the scrollery, the result of sixty years of painstaking effort and the hard work of twenty-four deputy ministers—and you saw fit to turn it all to ash?
Yu Cheng suddenly droops his head. He remains silent for what seems like ages. The Minister's eyes remain fixed on him, watching his every move.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: As I see it, it was no great loss.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Those files were filled with half-truths, whitewashed fabrications, and outright lies. Gazing upon them dirties the eyes; thinking of them taints the mind.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: So I thought it best to cleanse it all in flames.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Cleanse?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Just what are you trying to say?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: What am I trying to say? If you keen to know, then let's have a discussion: that which I burned, was it clean, or dirty?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Minister Chen, The suspect is clearly suffering from some sort of mental disease. It's getting late. Shall we conclude the questioning for today?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Escort Yu Cheng back to his cell.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: I truly regret that we subjected the Department of Discipline and Supervision to this circus here today.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: It is truly a vexing case. We understand.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: The Judicial Review Office will be sure to submit a full explanation to the Department of Discipline and Supervision.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Sigh... I just hope this can be resolved quickly, so I don't have to make so many trips here. You've planted way too many camphor trees in this courtyard—they're making me sneeze.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: I shall take my leave now, Deputy Minister Lin. See you.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: You should be off too, Lin Qingyan.
The courtroom door swings open, as sunlight pours in once more. Lin Qingyan immediately spots the seven towers with eighteen-pointed roofs hidden in the shadows of the trees.
The Judicial Review Office scrollery were all built in this style. The roofs of the towers seem to be covered with ash, the remnants of the burned southern section.
Just as she is about to step out the door, she hears a faint voice.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Lin Qingyan, it's almost time.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Do not forget.
Lin Qingyan steps out into the cold sunlight without even hesitating.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Achoo!

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Censor Jie Zhen, you're still here?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: I was waiting to chat with you for a minute. It's not convenient to talk in there.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: If you still want save... I mean... investigate Yu Cheng's case, you'd better move quickly.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: After the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies is over, all prisoners detained in Baizao will either be transferred to another prison or exiled. In any case, the cells must be emptied within two weeks.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Two weeks...

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: The imperial decree should reach you shortly. I just spotted it early, so I'm giving you a heads-up.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: And here I thought you didn't care much for these things.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: It is within my power to avoid caring, but you cannot get it out of your head. Yu Cheng is very important to you, isn't he?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: He was kind of like my teacher in the Judicial Review Office. He's the one who taught me to distinguish right from wrong.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: When I first discovered that he had fabricated evidence to convict a corrupt mandarin... well, I shrugged it off as 'using any means necessary to achieve justice.'

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: However, I never imagined he would set fire to the scrollery. There's absolutely no justice in that.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Indeed... I can't figure him out.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: But it does provoke a question... They've never emptied the jails for the Feast before. Why do it this year?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: This matter may not concern you directly, but I'm sure you've heard something about it?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Yumen experienced a Catastrophe at the beginning of the year. Then, this summer, we suffered the Dahuang incident.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: And what was the root cause of all this?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: ...The bestial Sui.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: This thousand-year-old case must finally be resolved...

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: I dare not engage in presumptuous speculation. This is as much as I can say for now.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Duoxie...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Censor Jie Zhen... why did you terminate the ongoing interrogation?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: As the saying goes, 'Words may deceive, so trust your eyes.'

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: I wager you haven't seen the burned scrollery yet.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: No, I have not.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Perhaps you'd better go see for yourself.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: I will take my leave.
The restaurant, which was loud and boisterous just a moment ago, goes completely silent.
The regulars, anticipating what is to come, file out of the diner one-by-one. Of course, they remember to leave money for their meals.

steps.name: Irritable Youth
steps.text: Jiang, close the door.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: ...*sigh*

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What? What happened?

steps.name: Irritable Youth
steps.text: Jiang, wasn't she just eating these tangerine cakes here?

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Yes, she was.

steps.name: Irritable Youth
steps.text: And didn't you tell me she was criticizing the taste?

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: No. She said they taste 'different', not bad, just 'different'.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: (winking vigorously)

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I guess you'd call it criticism. They're not exactly orthodox, different to what I had before.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: So you're the head chef, eh? Pretty young, aren't you?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Don't try to change the subject!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I was just critiquing the food. That's not a capital offense!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Besides, I thought the rest of the dishes were awesome.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Now you're on to flattery! This is my restaurant, and I have my rules! You either tell me what's wrong with the tangerine cakes, or I won't let you leave!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I told you already. They taste different to the ones I've had before.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Where, and when, did you eat them before?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Oh maybe... more than ten years ago? When I was living in Victoria, a relative sent them to me.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Did you come here to stir up trouble? Jiang! Escort her out!

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: No. We're not in the habit of kicking customers out of the restaurant...

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Good madam, think for a minute. What exactly is it about these cakes that tastes different? Maybe this is all some kind of misunderstanding?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Let me think... I remember the tangerine cakes I had before were sweeter. Yes, you must not have used enough sugar.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: The tangerine cakes need more sugar? Hahaha...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: To think I took you for a food critic. You are a woman with absolutely no taste. I won't waste my time arguing with you. Please leave.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You say I have no taste, when the real problem is your cooking?

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Oh... no...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: My cooking, you say?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Don't make me laugh! My cooking... my culinary talent, my—

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Alright then. I'll make you a bet. Go out this door here and sample the food at some of the other restaurants. If you find a better tasting meal, I'll give you this entire shop!

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: (softly) No, please no.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: But if you can't find better food, you have to sit at this table by the window and shout out to the streets...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Shout what?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Apologize to me! One hundred times!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: But what would I want with your restaurant?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Let's do this instead. If I find food that tastes better, then you'll let me eat here for a month, free, and you'll teach me how to cook a few of the tastiest dishes in Yanese cuisine, also free of charge.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: There's an old Yanese saying, 'Give a man a fin and you'll feed him for a day. Teach a man to fincatch, and you'll feed him for a lifetime.'

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: This restaurant... when I leave, I can't take it with me. If you teach me how to cook a few tasty dishes, I can cook them for my friends.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: But weren't you just criticizing my cooking?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I told you, all your other dishes taste great.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Wait. Wait a moment! Don't think you can just trick me like that! We still need to discuss the tangerine cakes!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Okay. Then I'll take your bet. I know I can find tangerine cakes, somewhere in Baizao, that taste like the ones I had before.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Huh? What's that weird smell?

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: I think it's coming from back in the kitchen...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I know that smell. It's like something is overcooked.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: My stew!

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Dear customer, I apologize. Our head chef has a bad temper and is easily offended.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Please come again, alright?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Pretty weird...

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: I've heard that skilled chefs tend to be eccentric.

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: In fact, I'll bet the reason he was able to become a good chef was precisely because he takes his food so seriously.

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: Did you notice that each of the five tofu dishes you ordered had tofu cut in a different way, yet every piece of tofu within each dish was exactly the same size and shape?

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: I don't think many chefs in Baizao could accomplish that.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Hm? You overheard our argument?

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: Sorry, I wasn't eavesdropping. You were just within earshot.

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: You were all having such fun, sharing your dishes amongst yourselves. Well, I believe you accidentally took the plate of tangerine cakes that I ordered.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Oh! Sorry about that!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What a dummy I was, taking someone else's food and then having a fight with the chef over it.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You wait here. I'll order you some more, straight away!

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: No. There's no need for that.

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: I came here today to try the food. After seeing how much you all enjoyed it, well, I figure it must be good enough.

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: However, I'm still a little curious, what exactly did you not like about the tangerine cakes?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I can't really put my finger on it, but I just know I've eaten better ones before.

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: Are you sure the dish you ate before was indeed 'tangerine cakes'?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Of course!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: One of my relatives lived in Baizao, and would ship me these cakes. There's no way I'd be wrong... I'm sure.

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: May I trouble you with a request, then?

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: You're going out looking for another restaurant that serves these tangerine cakes, right? Can you take me with you?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Sure! You're from Baizao, aren't you? That's perfect. You know your way around these parts!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Then again, it's getting kind of late. Let's meet here again tomorrow at noon. What do you say?

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: Certainly.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Oh, right. By the way, my name is Blaze. I'm a tourist from Victoria. How should I call you?

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: I am a woman of few hobbies. I like to write, and I like to eat.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: My pen name is 'The Wandering Foodie'. In any case, you may call me Xingzhu for short.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Such a trove of knowledge, those wonderful archives...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Ashes to ashes... dust to dust...
The dark space still has a lingering, acrid smell. On the collapsed beams of ironwood, murky raindrops tremble, ready to fall.
The iron chests that once held so many records and books have been warped and twisted by the flames. The paper and ink within have smoldered into ash, leaving only faint traces of words.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Do not linger too long. Rain showers after a fire send smoke up into the air.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: What have we learned so far?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: We've determined this to be arson.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: The absurd part? The fire's time and location match Yu Cheng's confession perfectly.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: The scrollery was heavily guarded, yet on the night of the fire, the guards didn't notice anything.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Not only was the perpetrator highly skilled in kung fu, but they also had intimate knowledge of the Judicial Review Office's layout. They must have been working with Yu Cheng for quite some time.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You're saying... you think this was an inside job?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: We cannot be certain.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: How bad was the damage?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: All records that were burned were from old cases, which has little effect on our current work. However, if these cases were ever to be reviewed in the future, there would be no evidence to go on.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Nearly all of these cases were Yu Cheng's responsibility.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Do you really believe Yu Cheng was the one who burned the scrollery?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Absolutely not...

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: No matter what nonsense he spouts, he was imprisoned when the fire broke out. There's no way he could have done it himself.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: However, I'm sure he's involved in some way. He's working with someone else.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: What did he mean when he suggested the files are 'dirty'?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Is there something on your mind?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Do you still remember... the last case Yu Cheng investigated before he retired?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: How could I forget?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Forty years ago, the Minister of Justice was stabbed in the street. The assassin turned out to be a mad beggar.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: The Judicial Review Office did everything in their power to uncover the man's identity, to no avail.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: In the end, they classified the murder as a random, spur-of-the moment act of violence.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: But nearly thirty years later, Yu Cheng accused the sitting Minister of Rites, Ning Shu, of being the murderer.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: I worked with Yu Cheng for many, many years. I knew him better than anyone.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: However, in his last few years at the Office, he began to change.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Something radicalized him. He began doing 'whatever it takes' to catch criminals. He even started fabricating evidence to close cold cases and settle old scores.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: If the accusations against him were baseless, then why did Minister Ning resign?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Do you still remember... Gu Quan?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: It all began when Gu Quan, serving as the envoy of ceremonial rites, died en route to Victoria...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Yu Cheng believed that Minister Ning murdered the Minister of Justice, and then killed the important witness in the case thirty years later.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: But that's the absurdity... the envoy had only just taken office. How could he have been connected to a case from thirty years prior?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Moreover, the envoy's manner, place, and time of death were all clearly established: he drowned near the Victorian border. How could the Minister of Rites have orchestrated his death, all the way from Baizao?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: The Judicial Review Office recorded Gu Quan's death in the case files...

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: The files are somewhere in this pile of ash that lays before you...

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Why raise these two cases now? Do you think they are connected to the fire somehow?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I would call it a hunch...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Yu Cheng's confession has drawn our attention, but clearly, there's some kind of larger scheme behind the fire. The real question isn't who set the fire, but the arsonist's ultimate goal.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Would you hand this case over to me?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: On what grounds?!

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Yu Cheng asked you to take notes during his trial. This is why you stand here now, and it is also the reason I cannot allow you to participate any further.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Whatever Yu Cheng's plan, you are most certainly a part of it.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: I know you regard him as a mentor and couldn't bear to see his reputation tarnished, but I will assign someone else to investigate the fire. Rest assured, we will get to the bottom of this.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: What about the cases that Yu Cheng once investigated?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: You'd best forget about those.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: No matter what you intend to investigate, it's simply not a good time.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Why do you say that?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Lin Qingyan, you are a Deputy Minister in the Judicial Review Office, not some patrolwoman. Every case you handle has a ripple effect.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Your so-called 'act of justice' may very well become a dagger in the hands of those with ulterior motives.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: So you know what's really going on with these cases, don't you?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Stay away from Yu Cheng's cases. That is my suggestion. Do not force me to make it an order.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Oh, and I have one final piece of advice...

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: You must learn to prioritize. The past is never as important as the present.
The young Deputy Minister is still standing in the same spot.
She walks down the path that's been cleared through the rubble, through the place that once held so many case files.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: The arsonist's motive is quite clear: he never wanted those files to see the light of day.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Whether Yu Cheng fabricated evidence or not, all available clues in both cases point to Ning Shu.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: But why would the Minister of Rites assassinate another high-ranking mandarin?
She bends down and brushes aside a charred beam, revealing a hint of green emerging from the ashes.
It's a pine tree.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Yu Cheng, you...

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: I planted this tree myself, right before I assumed my post in Baizao.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: After I die, cut down the tree. Use its wood to fashion my coffin.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Lin Qingyan, it's almost time.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Do not forget.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: This month's water bill is two thousand, and electricity is two thousand five hundred, while ingredient costs...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Go do your accounting somewhere else please. I can't stand you buzzing in my ear.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: According to my calculations, if you can come up with another three thousand, we'll be able to keep the doors open past this month.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: And where am I going to dig out that coin?

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: There are ways to do it—like the two months of meals owed by Wang the carpenter, or you can visit Shopkeeper Liu across the street and ask him for the balance he owes for last month's funeral banquet.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Collect enough of those outstanding debts, and we'll have what we need to make it through the month.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: That's... less than ideal... isn't it?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Customers on credit are in a tough spot. Going up to them and calling in the debt right now... feels awkward, to say the least.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: You want to play the good guy? Why, every time the rent collector comes calling, do you ask me to deal with him?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: You're... big-boned. Even if the rent-collector is angry, he won't take you in a fight.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Maybe... there's another way...

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Ding Feng Lou is coming here again today to hand out invitations to the competition.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: They're hiring chefs in preparation for the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies. If you can manage to win the competition, the prize money alone will be enough to pay our rent through the end of the year!

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: No! No way, no how!

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: I am the proud owner and head chef of 'Savors at Yu's'! How could I stoop so low as to work for someone else?

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: This is no ordinary cook! The head chef of Ding Feng Lou doesn't take apprentices, but even a casual demonstration provides enough to keep most chefs learning for three to five years. Plenty of people dream of working under him, never to get the chance!

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Besides, it's for the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies! The menu is recorded every year and passed down through generations. This is the lifelong dream of countless chefs—

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Those who want to attend are free to go. I shall not.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Are you scared?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: I'm not scared! You're scared!

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Hmmph. What Feast of a Hundred Delicacies? It's nothing more than a group of old gray-hairs hosting a big dinner party.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: All they ever talk is politics. They don't even have a chance to eat. It's a waste of time.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Just listen to your arrogance. You talk as if you've been there in person.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: I've catered so many banquets. They're all the same.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: You won't take any of my suggestions! I guess we're just going to let this restaurant fail then!

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Good grief, with a boss like you, I've got to start making new career plans.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Okay, okay. If it's just another three thousand we need, I'll start making extra deliveries each day through the end of the month.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: Have you no ambition? As a chef, don't you want your restaurant to do well? I'm not even sure why you opened it in the first place.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: People need to eat, which means there has to be someone to cook for them. As long as we have customers who want to eat my food, this restaurant will do just fine.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: More importantly, I promised I'd wait for a certain customer, and that one still haven't shown. I can't close the shop yet.

steps.name: Jiang
steps.text: What customer? Who do you need to wait for?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: It's just not time yet. A great stew demands patience. You have to add in the ingredients at just the right time.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: There's no need to rush.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What's with this thing? I can't get any channels. I want to watch the news!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Hey. You're back.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Indeed.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What have you learned?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I brought some food for you. I found a new restaurant today. The kitchen stinks to high heaven, but the cooking is pretty solid.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Oh, right, there's one other thing. Today I found these snacks that my dad once sent me a long time ago.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Who gave you permission to leave you room as you please?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Wha?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Seriously? I've been living off takeout for three days straight. I just wanted to go out and grab a bite to eat—is that not allowed?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: How many times have I told you? Your identity and status are extremely important; your current situation is dreadfully tenuous. Are you taking this seriously or not?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Lin Qingyan! Are you off your rocker? We already established the three rules. No one said I was confined to my room!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I had a good life back at Rhodes Island. Then you showed up and told me my father's death was suspicious, without giving any details.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I came all the way here to Baizao, the place where my dad used to live, and you still haven't told me anything! You've made me stay in this room, day after day, and now you have the gall to yell at me?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I... that is—

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Forgive me. I should not have scolded you. The current situation is not as I had anticipated.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What 'situation'? Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I don't know. A lot of unexpected things happened in Baizao before we arrived.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: If you would aid me, then simply do what you can to avoid danger, understood?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: As for your father, I just happened to be handed that case a few years ago.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: The case was originally being handled by my predecessor, someone I trusted deeply. Your father seemed to have been spending a lot of time pursuing a certain 'truth' in the last few years of his life.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: His death was suspicious. Every clue we've found hints that there were larger forces at work there. How large? We don't know for certain, nor can we even hope to guess.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: But your mere existence is the most important piece of evidence we have.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Blaze, I vow to you I will find the truth, and once I do, I will tell you everything.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: However, until I do, I simply need you to trust me. I need you to cooperate with me.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: By the way, what were you saying about your father just now?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I said I found these snacks that he used to send to me a long time ago.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: And?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: They don't taste the same as they used to. Maybe it's just because I'm remembering wrong.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: The Yanese have a saying for this, right? 'The situation remains the same, yet the people have changed.'

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: No. That's not right. The situation has also changed.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Well then, a more apt saying would be, 'Times change, and with them, change all things.'

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Too much time has passed. It will be very hard for us to find any clues left from back then.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: But these are in fact one of the few things I've found in Baizao that relates to my father.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: When I lived with my mother in Victoria, my dad would send them to me from time to time.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I figured that by the time I got my disease under control and figured out what I really believed in, my dad would be back in Victoria, waiting for me to come home. Naive.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Everyone longs for that sort of 'happy ending'.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: And yet, by the time I found a place that could treat my Oripathy and finished some of the things I had to do with the bunny's crew... my dad... was gone.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Before you came and found me, I always thought my dad's death was an accident. I was sad, but there was nothing I could do about it.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: But if you're telling me my father was murdered.... then that's an entirely different story.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I need to learn the truth. I owe that to my father... and myself.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: In all truth, I know very little about what happened to your father. Many of the old archives have been lost, and very little information can be extracted from what remains.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Just from looking at the case files he left behind, we can see that your father worked as a ceremonial officer in the Ministry of Rites for over ten years but never got promoted. It seems he was not well-suited to serve in public office.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: However, to stay in a position like that for over a decade... he must have been a good person.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Good people... good people also die.
She walks over to the window, closes her eyes, and rubs her temples.
The faraway city lights are shimmering in the twilight. The years of wandering are long over.
People today are moving from one stage of life to the next, as the city guides them and runs right behind them.
Many boundaries are blurred, many high walls become thoroughfares, many hurried footsteps pass over the paving stones. Not everyone is qualified to etch their name into the annals of history.
